strings.name: Hito Steyerl
strings.summary: Steyerl developed film training into installations combining documentary, fiction and lectures, asking how images circulate through war, capital and digital platforms. How Not to Be Seen and Factory of the Sun turn viewing itself into a political question. Alongside writing and teaching, recent work addresses artificial intelligence, drones and climate crisis.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Uses video installations and theoretical writing on digital images, war and capital to shape contemporary art's thinking about technology and social structures.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Film education in Tokyo and Munich; philosophy PhD from the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna.
strings.highlights.h1.title: How viewing is organized
strings.highlights.h1.text: Turns tutorials, games and documentary material into installations questioning visibility, surveillance and labor.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Theory alongside production
strings.highlights.h2.text: Books including Duty Free Art connect art institutions, finance and global conflict.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Major Hamburg exhibition opened
strings.timeline.t1.text: Deichtorhallen assembled installations made between 1999 and 2025, including The Island.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Released new technological critiques
strings.timeline.t2.text: Mechanical Kurds addressed drone and AI warfare; The Island linked flooding, science and politics.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Exhibited Power Plants
strings.timeline.t3.text: The Serpentine exhibition in London connected digital prediction, augmented reality and urban inequality.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Published Duty Free Art
strings.timeline.t4.text: The essays examined global conflict, capital flows and contemporary art institutions.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Factory of the Sun presented
strings.timeline.t5.text: Shown in the German pavilion at Venice, it used game-like images to examine labor and control.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Made How Not to Be Seen
strings.timeline.t6.text: A satirical instructional video explored becoming visible or invisible under digital surveillance.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Lovely Andrea entered documenta
strings.timeline.t7.text: The film was shown at documenta 12 in Kassel, linking personal image history and power.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Participated in Manifesta 5
strings.timeline.t8.text: An early international exhibition brought her film and art practice into Europe's biennial network.
